reason: The dome and lens both bend light, so combining them seems like a useful start on focusing the image.
expectation: I expect a focusing part of the eye, though the iris may still need to be added to control light.

alternatives.reason: The light-sensitive cells and nerve cells could start the separate signal pathway, but I want to build the focusing front first.

effect: The dome and lens focus light toward the back; the iris is still needed to control how much enters.
reaction: The converging rays make the two parts' shared job clear.
reason: I'll add the iris to finish the light-controlling part of the eye front.
expectation: I expect the iris to add an adjustable opening that controls incoming light.

alternatives.reason: I could build the light-sensitive pathway first, but I want to finish the eye front.

effect: The eye front is complete: the iris controls incoming light, while the dome and lens focus it.
reaction: The picture makes the different jobs of the parts clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it starts the remaining light-sensitive lining and nerve goal.
expectation: I expect the light-sensitive cells to connect to nerve fibres that carry signals, though I don't know exactly what the result will be called.

effect: The lining is called the retina, and its nerve fibres gather into the optic nerve. Now the front and lining need to be joined.
reaction: The picture makes the outgoing bundle easy to understand.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it brings the focusing and sensing parts together.
expectation: I expect an eye cutaway with light focused onto the retina and the optic nerve leading away from it.

effect: The completed eye shows how the front focuses light onto the retina and the optic nerve carries information toward the brain.
reaction: Seeing the two projects come together around the leaf was satisfying and made the pathway clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the eye front and retina was most worthwhile because the finished cutaway connected focusing light with sending information toward the brain.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the iris was clear but fairly predictable after seeing its picture and the goal.

surprise.text: I learned that the light-sensitive lining is called the retina and that its nerve fibres gather into the optic nerve.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained the parts' purposes, although the last two combinations were the only offered actions.

continue.text: I would continue: assembling the eye made me curious how another body system's parts work together, though the later choices here were limited.
